title: Trump's $100K Branded Watches Sold via Campaign in 2024
description_short: Trump's $100K Branded Watches Sold via Campaign in 2024
description_medium: Trump-branded watches were marketed during the 2024 campaign at prices reaching $100,000 through a private merchandise venture. The luxury products blended Trump’s political identity with commercial sales, raising questions about revenue disclosure and who benefited. Their sale highlighted the challenge of separating campaign-era promotion from private business.
description_long: During the 2024 campaign, Trump-branded watches were marketed for as much as $100,000 through a private merchandise venture. The luxury products were promoted to supporters alongside Trump’s political identity, blending celebrity branding with campaign-era attention. The watches were not ordinary campaign contributions: buyers were purchasing a commercial product, and the arrangement raised questions about how the venture’s revenue was disclosed and who benefited financially. The sale illustrated Trump’s ability to monetize his name and political following while running for office. It also highlighted the difficulty of distinguishing campaign fundraising from private business when products are marketed to voters and supporters. The price point limited the market to wealthy buyers, while the broader promotional strategy turned political loyalty into a consumer product. The episode prompted scrutiny of financial transparency and potential conflicts, though the existence of high-priced merchandise alone does not establish a violation of campaign-finance law.

title: Trump: Michael Cohen threatens Daily Beast reporter on behalf of Donald Trump
description_short: Trump: Michael Cohen threatens Daily Beast reporter on behalf of Donald Trump
description_medium: Michael Cohen, then Donald Trump’s lawyer, threatened Daily Beast reporter Tim Mak with a costly lawsuit and personal ruin if he published a story about Ivana Trump’s rape allegation. The Daily Beast published the story and Cohen’s threats. Ivana Trump later said she had not meant “rape” literally, and Trump denied the allegation.
description_long: In July 2015, Daily Beast reporter Tim Mak was preparing a story about Ivana Trump’s allegation that Donald Trump had raped her during their marriage. Trump’s attorney Michael Cohen called Mak and threatened to sue him and financially ruin him if the article used Trump’s name alongside the word “rape.” Cohen also warned that the reporter would face personal consequences for publishing the story. The Daily Beast published the article and Cohen’s threats. The episode raised a press-freedom concern because a lawyer for a powerful presidential candidate used threats of litigation and personal harm to deter reporting on a serious allegation. Ivana Trump later said she had not meant “rape” in a criminal or literal sense, and Trump denied the allegation. Those distinctions matter when describing the underlying claim. The threats themselves were documented in the reporter’s account and Cohen’s recorded remarks. They illustrate how legal intimidation can be used to pressure journalists even when a story is ultimately published.
